title: Product network fault profiles
purpose: Reusable test plans. A profile definition or a passing synthetic lab is not product coverage.

execution_contract.authority: Use the current task's authorized target, environment, data and effect scope. Skill installation is not product-test authorization.
execution_contract.budgets: Choose explicit request, retry, concurrency, duration and stop limits before execution; do not use unlimited retries.
execution_contract.isolation: Keep control/evidence traffic outside the injected fault path. Use disposable owned fixtures and clean up only owned state.
execution_contract.independent_oracle: Query actual persisted effects, job state, output files or authoritative server data separately from client UI/HTTP success.
execution_contract.lab_scope: The bundled runner is loopback-only, synthetic HTTP/SQLite, five scenario IDs; remaining profiles are adapter recipes.

profiles.name: Offline before submission
profiles.fault: Refuse connection before a request reaches the service.
invariants: No committed effect before recovery.
The same intended operation can complete once after recovery.
independent_oracles: Inspect committed data before reconnect and after one retry.
Observe the client state; queued is distinct from completed.
profiles.recovery: Restore only the test connection; reconcile and retry within a fixed budget.
profiles.limits: The bundled lab proves no request delivery before recovery and committed-effect counts, not offline browser/native UI.

profiles.name: Disconnect during upload or streaming request
profiles.fault: Cut the selected connection after a known partial request/body checkpoint.
invariants: Partial input cannot appear as a complete saved object.
Resume/retry follows the specified checksum/offset/idempotency contract.
independent_oracles: Inspect actual stored object size/checksum and operation record.
Record bytes/checkpoint and confirm the injected disconnect occurred.
profiles.recovery: Remove the disconnect rule; resume or retry and verify exactly the intended complete result.
profiles.limits: Requires product-specific resumable protocol and storage oracle; the bundled lab does not execute this profile.

profiles.name: Latency, jitter and limited bandwidth
profiles.fault: Apply bounded delay/jitter/bandwidth to an explicit test path.
invariants: Progress and timeout state reflect the operation's real status.
Queues and retries remain within the declared budget.
independent_oracles: Capture adapter counters and request timeline.
Inspect pending work and committed effects independently of the spinner.
profiles.recovery: Remove the limit; verify backlog drains and normal latency returns.
profiles.limits: Use separate control traffic; choose values from actual product latency budgets.

profiles.name: Committed effect then lost response
profiles.fault: Drop the response after a durable side effect commits.
invariants: A timeout/lost reply leaves outcome unknown until reconciled.
Retrying the same operation identity must not duplicate the effect.
independent_oracles: Query the committed effects before retry.
Reconcile through a durable operation record and count effects after retry.
profiles.recovery: Restore transport; return the prior result or reconcile before any repeated side effect.
profiles.limits: The lab uses real local HTTP and SQLite; an API success response alone is not its oracle.

profiles.name: Response timeout after commit
profiles.fault: Delay a response beyond the client's bounded deadline after durable commit.
invariants: Timeout does not imply rollback.
A permitted retry or reconciliation produces only the intended effect.
independent_oracles: Check first operation committed before retry.
Measure actual timeout and inspect persistent effects after recovery.
profiles.recovery: Remove delay; reconcile using the same operation identity.
profiles.limits: The lab uses a 0.35-second delayed response and 0.10-second caller timeout; production values must follow product budgets.

profiles.name: DNS resolution failure
profiles.fault: Fail resolution for an owned test hostname.
invariants: The app reports the affected service accurately.
Recovery does not require deleting unrelated state or credentials.
independent_oracles: Confirm resolver failure on the actual request path.
Check retry count, application error state and state persistence.
profiles.recovery: Restore the test resolver; verify subsequent operations recover.
profiles.limits: Never modify the owner's system DNS to simulate this profile; not executed by the bundled lab.

profiles.name: TLS/certificate handshake failure
profiles.fault: Serve an owned fixture with the specifically invalid/expired/untrusted certificate scenario.
invariants: The app does not silently bypass certificate verification.
The user sees an accurate failure with no false completion.
independent_oracles: Record handshake failure without capturing secrets.
Inspect committed effect count and trust behavior.
profiles.recovery: Restore the valid fixture certificate/trust arrangement; rerun the normal flow.
profiles.limits: Use disposable test trust configuration; certificate pinning may require dedicated fixture design.

profiles.name: TCP reset or truncated response
profiles.fault: Reset the selected connection or truncate a defined response part.
invariants: Incomplete content cannot be marked as valid/complete.
Retries are bounded and cannot duplicate mutating effects.
independent_oracles: Verify the actual reset/truncation and parse/checksum result.
Inspect durable operation state separately from transport failure.
profiles.recovery: Remove fault; fetch/reconcile successfully and verify content integrity.
profiles.limits: TCP stream truncation is not genuine network packet loss.

profiles.name: Rate limit then recovery
profiles.fault: Return 429 before applying the operation, with a declared Retry-After.
invariants: A rejected attempt has no side effect.
Retry count and timing obey the specified bounded policy.
independent_oracles: Inspect effects before retry.
Record response status, Retry-After, retry timeline and total attempts.
profiles.recovery: Allow a later attempt; verify one effect and no runaway queue.
profiles.limits: The lab specifically tests Retry-After=0 and one retry; general backoff/jitter needs a product adapter.

profiles.name: 503 and partial dependency outage
profiles.fault: Fail one scoped dependency while independent capabilities remain available.
invariants: Dependent operations have accurate partial-failure state.
Independent product functions continue if the product contract requires it.
independent_oracles: Observe both dependent and independent flows.
Inspect queues, durable state, error classification and recovery counters.
profiles.recovery: Restore the dependency; drain/reconcile bounded work without duplicating effects.
profiles.limits: Do not infer whole-product failure from a single mocked dependency response.

profiles.name: WebSocket disconnect and reconnect
profiles.fault: Interrupt the actual event connection, then permit bounded reconnection.
invariants: Reconnect loops respect budgets.
The final client state matches authoritative server state.
independent_oracles: Capture connection transitions and last acknowledged event/state version.
Compare post-reconnect client state against server data.
profiles.recovery: Restore the event connection; verify replay or snapshot reconciliation completes.
profiles.limits: HTTP fixture success does not validate WebSockets; verify installed adapter support.

profiles.name: Duplicate, delayed or out-of-order events
profiles.fault: Deliver a known event sequence with duplicates, omissions and reordering.
invariants: An event's effect is not applied twice.
Version/order reconciliation matches the product event contract.
independent_oracles: Record emitted event identities/versions.
Compare materialized state to an independent expected model.
profiles.recovery: Resume normal events; reconcile missing state and verify stable convergence.
profiles.limits: Do not assume every event protocol guarantees ordered delivery or replay.

profiles.name: Queue pressure and retry amplification
profiles.fault: Apply bounded traffic while an owned downstream path is slow/unavailable.
invariants: Workload/backpressure follow explicit queue limits.
Retries do not multiply side effects or exceed the allowed budget.
independent_oracles: Measure input rate, completed rate, dropped/queued work and retry count.
Inspect unique operation IDs and committed effects.
profiles.recovery: Remove the fault; verify drain time, resource recovery and no duplicate application.
profiles.limits: Check load-generator headroom; closed-loop traffic can conceal arrival-rate pressure.

profiles.name: Native sleep/wake and network switching
profiles.fault: Suspend/resume a test device or switch its controlled Wi-Fi/VPN path mid-flow.
invariants: Session and operation state remain truthful across lifecycle changes.
Recovery does not duplicate the interrupted action.
independent_oracles: Record device lifecycle/network transition and task identity.
Inspect native UI, persisted state and server operation record.
profiles.recovery: Restore the known network/session; reconcile pending work.
profiles.limits: Use an authorized test device; do not sleep or disconnect the owner's control Mac as a fixture.

profiles.name: Cancellation with a late response
profiles.fault: Delay completion, request cancellation, then release a late result.
invariants: Cancellation behavior matches the documented commit boundary.
Late results cannot silently overwrite newer user state.
independent_oracles: Inspect background job and durable effect state.
Compare UI cancellation state and final operation status.
profiles.recovery: Release the delay; confirm final state or an explicit committed-before-cancel outcome.
profiles.limits: Cancellation is not necessarily rollback; define the product rule before testing.

profiles.name: Expired credentials or role change during a request
profiles.fault: Expire/revoke a test credential or change an authorized test role at a defined boundary.
invariants: Server-side access decisions remain correct.
Retries/fallback cannot retain stale privilege or expose another identity's data.
independent_oracles: Use separate peer identities and direct API/storage checks.
Inspect actual returned/persisted data and refreshed token/session state.
profiles.recovery: Restore only owned test identity configuration; verify the new policy consistently.
profiles.limits: A hidden UI control or HTTP status alone does not prove data isolation.

profiles.name: Lost reply and server restart
profiles.fault: Commit an operation, lose its reply, and recreate the service before retry.
invariants: Operation identity and deduplication survive server memory loss.
Retry does not duplicate the durable effect.
independent_oracles: Read committed effects before and after restart/retry.
Verify fresh service instances retrieve the durable operation record.
profiles.recovery: Start the owned test service and reconcile the same operation identity.
profiles.limits: The lab recreates HTTP server and Store objects with the same SQLite file; it does not kill an OS process or simulate power loss.

profiles.name: Long-running connection/resource soak
profiles.fault: Run a bounded representative workload and repeated reconnects over a declared duration.
invariants: Memory, descriptors, connections and temporary data stay within defined budgets.
Latency/error rate and data correctness remain acceptable over time.
independent_oracles: Collect time-series resource and service metrics.
Sample independent operation/effect consistency and real output integrity.
profiles.recovery: Stop the owned workload; verify resources return to the specified steady state.
profiles.limits: A short lab or small MCP run cannot stand in for a genuine soak test.

profiles.name: Genuine packet loss, duplication and reordering
profiles.fault: Apply scoped IP packet loss/reordering/duplication on an owned isolated interface.
invariants: The app's actual protocol recovers within its contract.
No false success, unbounded retries or repeated side effects occur.
independent_oracles: Record interface/direction, netem settings and packet/counter evidence.
Inspect endpoint state and operation results independently.
profiles.recovery: Remove only the owned rules; prove normal routing and behavior return.
profiles.limits: TCP stream fault injection is not equivalent; UDP/QUIC needs a real packet-level path.

profiles.name: Fault removal and full recovery
profiles.fault: Remove the prior fault after recording its effect on the system.
invariants: Normal behavior returns without undocumented manual reset.
No stale queue, reconnect loop, resource leak or hidden duplicate effect remains.
independent_oracles: Repeat the baseline journey on the same observed build.
Compare operation records, queue/resource trends and UI/server state.
profiles.recovery: Verify owned adapter/process cleanup and preserve original failure evidence.
profiles.limits: This must accompany each executed product fault profile; lab fixture cleanup alone is not product recovery.
